title: The ordinary scalar tensor comparison preserves insertion of one
statement: Let (C,T) be a small site, f:R→S a map of commutative ring sheaves, P any unbounded R-module-sheaf complex, and B_f the restricted rank-one S-module. For the explicit ordinary comparison c_f(P) of [lem-sfb-ringed-scalar-tensor-comparison], the right-unitor inverse P→P tensor_R R[0], followed by tensoring the map R[0]→B_f[0] corresponding to the section one, and then c_f(P), equals the termwise scalar adjunction unit P→res_f(change_f(P)) of [lem-sfb-adic-finite-reduction-data]. No derived category, K-flatness, tower, limit, or flatness hypothesis occurs.

source.place: Section tensor-product (03EK), the sheafified tensor formulas; lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict (03CZ), scalar adjunction. For derived comparisons: sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-derived-base-change (06YY). For quotient transitions: proetale.tex, lemma-naive-completion (099M).

proof.text: In each degree contract the sole nonzero (q,0) summand. The ordinary right unitor inverse sends x to x tensor 1; the tensor map preserves this formula. Symmetry sends this to 1 tensor x. By the section normalization of cancellation its inverse sends this to 1 tensor (1 tensor x), and the left unitor sends it to 1 tensor x. Sheafification adjunction and tensor induction justify the local-section calculation. The ordinary scalar unit is the same insertion by its normalization.
